plan.p0: A plausible mechanism is to detect four same-colored corner markers, keep them fixed, and translate every other colored cell into the rectangle’s strict interior while preserving relative geometry. The payload is scaled neither in color nor shape; the translation is whatever is needed to fit it inside. This assumes all non-marker cells belong to one payload.
plan.p1: A plausible mechanism is to treat the marked rectangle as a slot and center the payload’s bounding box within that slot, preserving its internal coordinates. In the examples this places the horizontal string on the sole interior row and shifts the narrow vertical pattern down one row. This assumes centering, rather than merely moving toward the nearest boundary.
plan.p2: A plausible mechanism is inward gravity: retain the four markers, then translate the entire non-marker pattern along the rectangle’s short axis until no payload cell lies on or beyond a marker line. The horizontal case moves downward to the middle; the narrow case moves down one cell. This predicts no repacking of disconnected pieces.
plan.p3: A plausible mechanism is serialization: read all non-marker colors in row-major order and rewrite that sequence row-major into the rectangle’s strict interior, leaving markers unchanged. It matches the preserved color order in both outputs but would differ from geometric translation when the payload has holes, multiple rows, or disconnected components.
